articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Information Technology - Engineering the Future' (Digest No.23)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Information Technology - Engineering the Future
IEE Colloquium on Information Technology - Engineering the Future
abstract: Throughout the technologically advanced nations there is now a massive restructuring of the manufacturing base. This restructuring displays three predominant characteristics: there is a change in the organic composition of capital as processes are rendered capital intensive rather than labour intensive; there is a shift from the analogical to the digital; it is a process in which human beings are rendered passive and the systems become more active. The effects of these tendencies are outlined. Problems and opportunities are discussed, including effects on employment patterns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Information Technology - Engineering the Future
abstract: The new information technology paradigm, based on a constellation of industries, which are among the fastest growing in all the leading industrial countries, such as computers, electronic components and telecommunications, has already resulted in a drastic fall in costs and a counter-inflationary trend in prices in these sectors as well as vastly improved technical performance. This combination is relatively rare in the history of technology and it means that this new technological system satisfies all the requirements for a Schumpeterian revolution in the economy. The author discusses economic issues in information technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
